02 · The problem
Two sides of one fragmented market
TRAVELERS
They assemble the journey alone
Tashkent → Almaty means weighing, across services and countries:
Departure and arrival times
Prices and availability
Total journey duration
Transfers and waiting
Local transport to stations
Border-crossing rules
Is the route practical?
OPERATORS
They run on manual tools
Manual reservations · inconsistent seat records · limited reporting · scattered customer data · hard-to-track vehicle and driver assignments · low digital visibility
To be validated through direct operator interviews

03 · The T-Port solution
One starting point for the whole journey
TRAVELER
"I need to travel from Tashkent to Bukhara tomorrow. Find an affordable option with minimal waiting time."
Core value
Fragmented transport information, turned into a clear, practical journey plan.
T-PORT
Compares train, flight, bus and other supported options
Shows verified prices and schedules where available
Estimates total journey duration
Identifies required transfers
Ranks alternatives by the traveler's priorities
Links to providers for final checks and booking

04 / 20
04 · Product ecosystem
Four products, one platform
B2C
T-Port Travel
Unified search, journey comparison, multimodal routes, smart recommendations, saved journeys, external booking links.
AI
T-Port Intelligence
Plan in natural language. It interprets the request, applies preferences and explains the alternatives.
ALERTS
Ticket Sniper
Watches permitted sources, sends Telegram or web alerts, links to the provider. Alerts — not automated buying.
B2B
T-Port Fleet
Web-CRM for vehicles, drivers, routes, seat inventory, reservations, dispatch and reporting.
Plus T-Port Workspace — internal tools for data sources, monitoring, subscriptions, analytics, security and support.

05 · T-Port Intelligence
AI interprets. Software verifies.
ASK IN PLAIN WORDS
"Find the cheapest practical way to Samarkand."
"I want to arrive before noon."
"Avoid transfers shorter than 30 minutes."
"Compare the fastest and most affordable."
Language model
Understands requests, extracts preferences, explains options
Provider-data adapters
Schedules, prices and availability from permitted sources
Deterministic logic
Durations, transfers and validation
AI never invents availability, prices or schedules.

07 / 20
07 · Competitive strategy
Built around the journey, not the ticket
Ticketing sites, airline search, mobility and travel apps already exist. T-Port tests whether organizing them around the complete trip adds value.
Journey-level thinking
Origin to destination, not one ticket.
Multimodal planning
Combinations of transport where data allows.
Natural language
Describe preferences instead of filters.
Clear comparisons
Trade-offs between price, time and transfers.
A potential B2B layer
Fleet software for operators who want it.
Intended differentiators, not yet proven advantages — to be shown through a working product and user research.
T-PORT
· The Global Transit Gateway

08 / 20
08 · Go-to-market
Five phases, each earned by the last
PHASE 1
Build and validate
Free MVP, limited routes, reliable sources. Prove successful searches and repeat use.
PHASE 2
Organic distribution
SEO route pages, city guides, Telegram bot, social demos, student communities, referrals.
PHASE 3
Test Premium
A paid plan built from usage data — without gutting the free core.
PHASE 4
Pilot Fleet
Interview operators, pilot with willing customers, prove time saved.
PHASE 5
Expand when justified
More routes and markets once data, reliability, demand and capital allow.

13 · Five-year roadmap
Local proof first, then the region
YEAR 1
Establish Uzbekistan
Prove people need and reuse T-Port.
MVP · permitted data · test Premium · operator interviews · Fleet pilot if demanded
YEAR 2
Product and revenue
Repeatable B2C revenue and a validated B2B offer.
Coverage · refine Premium · alerts · paying Fleet pilots
YEAR 3
Central Asia
Evaluate Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan.
Demand · data · payments · regulation · language — market by market
YEAR 4
Regional platform
Strengthen tech and operations.
New corridors · mature Fleet · localization · selected integrations
YEAR 5
Evaluate global
Corridors to Türkiye, UAE, Saudi Arabia, China.
Each needs its own validation and compliance
A $1B valuation is a long-term ambition, not an assumed outcome — it must be earned through scale and durable revenue.

14 · Technology
A modular architecture
EXPERIENCE
Next.js · TypeScript — responsive web app and PWA
AI LAYER
Language models — understand requests, extract preferences, explain options
CORE
Python · FastAPI — search orchestration, users, subscriptions, business logic
DATA
PostgreSQL · Redis + workers · provider adapters — PostGIS when spatial search justifies it
DELIVERY
Telegram · web notifications — for supported alerts
Principle: natural-language interpretation stays separate from route calculation and factual data.

15 · Data access and legal
Permitted data only
Official APIs, permitted public information and authorized sources.
No scraping without permission, no bypassing access controls. Legal classification, personal data and hosting reviewed under Uzbek law before launch.
BEFORE ANY SOURCE IS ADDED
Terms of service and data-use rights
Technical access restrictions
Attribution requirements
Accuracy and update frequency
Privacy implications
Transport and consumer-protection rules
PLANNED
Partnership with the Ministry of Transport via the President AI Award initiative — to integrate official state transport APIs into one AI-driven mobility gateway.

16 · Defensibility
The moat is execution
A search interface alone is not a durable advantage.
Journey intelligence
A consistent way to compare whole journeys.
Data normalization
Reliable processes across many permitted sources.
User experience
A simple interface for a complex problem.
Retention
Saved preferences, useful alerts, repeat planning.
Operator software
Fleet tools businesses choose to keep using.
Regional expertise
Routes, transfer limits and local needs.

17 / 20
17 · Key risks
Risks we plan around
Risk
Mitigation
Insufficient data access
Start with a few permitted sources and routes; expand only when coverage holds
Low willingness to pay
Test features and pricing before Premium carries the cost structure
Competition
Focus on complete journeys, data quality, usability and proven features
Expensive acquisition
Track CAC, organic growth, retention and LTV before paid marketing
B2B adoption
Interview operators, run small pilots, build only for validated problems
Wrong journey info
Validate data, show timestamps and uncertainty, deterministic calculations
Legal complexity
Review each market and business activity separately before launch
